key_insight: A fast reduced gas-dynamic model captures post-pulse gas expansion more accurately than existing closures, which can substantially overestimate density, temperature and reactive species.
engineering_relevance: Improved expansion modeling helps predict the gas density and energy per molecule encountered by successive pulses in high-repetition-rate plasma systems.
method: Represent radial gas expansion with Lagrangian shells.
Close the model with an approximate cylindrical acoustic radiation condition, without fitted physical coefficients.
Couple gas dynamics to the SoPlasma-0D global plasma-kinetics solver.
evidence_signal: For smooth deposition profiles and axis pressures up to six times ambient, the reduced model reproduces verified 1D compressible CFD axis densities within 2.4%, typically running about 1,000 times faster.
watch_item: Accuracy beyond the tested smooth deposition profiles and pressure range requires further validation.
paper_title: Gas expansion in global models of nanosecond pulsed discharges: a reduced gas-dynamic model coupled to plasma kinetics
